_schema._comment: submissions.json — the state of student work. FOUR flat append-mostly arrays joined on learner_id + case_id. WRITE OWNERSHIP IS SPLIT BY ARRAY, and only by array: assignments[], submissions[] and discussions[] are written ONLY by case-track; scores[] is written ONLY by submission-score. No skill writes an array it does not own. Nothing case-track records is a grade: it records state and flags what needs human judgment. Nothing submission-score writes is final: every score is `machine-first-pass` until a guide confirms it.

assignment_fields.due_on: ISO date or null. null = no deadline; such an assignment can never be OVERDUE, only STALE.
assignment_fields.badge_index: integer or null. Which badge slot this case is intended to count toward. null = unallocated; case-track will flag it once the case completes.
assignment_fields.status: enum: assigned | submitted | reviewed | complete | withdrawn. Transitions are one-way except withdrawn. 'complete' requires reviewed AND discussion_count >= 2 and is set only by an explicit human confirm in case-track.

submission_fields.id: string. '<assignment_id>__sub<N>'. Resubmissions get a new record; the old one is retained.
submission_fields.artifacts: object mirroring the fixed five Challenges: {challenge_1_resource_url (string|null), challenge_2_pitch_url (string|null), challenge_2_word_count (int|null), challenge_2_has_original_visual (bool|null), challenge_3_deliverables_present (array of deliverable ids from case.json), challenge_4_appendix_url (string|null)}. null means NOT RECORDED, which is different from absent — case-track reports it as unknown, never as a zero.
submission_fields.source: enum: facilitator-dictated | drive-intake. How this record entered the system (Roadmap C3). 'facilitator-dictated' is a human reading the Hero's actual posts and telling case-track the links/counts directly — the original and still the default path. 'drive-intake' means case-track found new files in the learner's Drive submissions folder (see roster.json drive_folder_id and skills/case-track/SKILL.md 'Drive intake') and staged this record from that — it still requires the same human confirm before writing, and it does NOT set reviewed_on/outcome by itself; a file arriving is not a review happening.
submission_fields.drive_artifacts: object or null. Present only when source == 'drive-intake': {folder_id (string), files: [{drive_file_id, name, modified_time (ISO), local_path (string, relative to project root)}]}. local_path is where case-track downloaded a copy under student_work/<learner_id>/<case_id>/submitted/ — Drive is the intake channel, never treated as the artifact's only copy, so downstream tools (e.g. submission-score --file) always have a local path to read.
submission_fields.reviewed_on: ISO date or null. null = AWAITING REVIEW in the exception queue.
submission_fields.review_note: string or null. Free-text facilitator judgment. There is no numeric score field by design.
submission_fields.outcome: enum or null: accepted | revise | not-accepted. Human-set. null until reviewed.

discussion_fields.mode: enum: live | written-500. 'written-500' is the SPEC Challenge 5 absence substitute (500 excellent words on the discussion questions).

invariants: Challenge 5 requires TWO discussion records per learner per case. discussion_count < 2 blocks 'complete'.
A case counts toward a badge only when its assignment status == 'complete'.
Nothing in this file is computed on write. Badge progress, overdue state and the exception queue are DERIVED by case-track at read time from these three arrays plus roster.json.
Records with _example: true are seed data for rendering only and are excluded from every count.
A score record with status 'machine-first-pass' never contributes to badge progress. case-track must treat it as INTERIM.
badge_eligible and growth_score are DERIVED from criteria[] and are recomputed, never hand-set.
Every entry in overrides[] has a matching row in readmodel/score_overrides.json. Overrides are the training signal; a dropped override is lost calibration data.
A drive-intake submission's presence in Drive never sets reviewed_on or outcome — those stay human-only regardless of source (MCS-40).

score_fields._comment: Written ONLY by skills/submission-score/. score_submission.py creates the record with status 'machine-first-pass'; guide_confirm.py is the only writer that may set status 'confirmed'. A machine-first-pass record does NOT count toward a badge and renders as INTERIM on the dashboard.
score_fields.id: string. '<learner_id>__<case_id>__<scored_on>'. Unique. A rescore on the same day replaces; a rescore on a later day is a new record and the old one is retained.
score_fields.status: enum: machine-first-pass | confirmed. RUBRIC hard limit 3. Only guide_confirm.py sets 'confirmed'. There is no 'rejected' state — a guide who disagrees overrides the criterion and confirms, so the disagreement is captured as a training signal rather than discarded.
score_fields.criteria: object C1..C7 -> {level: 'Not Yet'|'Proficient'|'Exemplary', confidence: 'HIGH'|'MEDIUM'|'LOW', set_by?: 'guide'}. RUBRIC hard limit 2: C7 is never 'Exemplary' unless set_by == 'guide'.
score_fields.badge_eligible: bool. THE MASTERY GATE: all seven criteria >= Proficient. No partial credit, no compensation. Recomputed on confirm.
score_fields.growth_score: number 0-100. Weighted C1..C7 at 5/20/20/15/15/15/10, Not Yet 0 / Proficient 70 / Exemplary 100. NEVER averaged with the mastery gate, never shown to a learner as a grade, never used for badge eligibility. It exists so a guide can see 61 -> 68 -> 74 across three cases.
score_fields.surface_first: array of criterion ids the machine flagged LOW confidence. The guide reads these first; they are not buried.
score_fields.confirmed_by: string or null. Named human. null while status is machine-first-pass.
score_fields.overrides: array of {criterion, from, to, reason}. Mirrors the rows appended to readmodel/score_overrides.json, which is the file the bias audit reads.

submissions.review_note: Strong first submission. C2 and C7 read as genuine, not cue-phrase luck -- she names the trade-off explicitly and answers the strongest counter-argument rather than just naming it. D5's equation is solved correctly and the round-up logic is checked both ways (122 falls short, 123 clears). Overrode C3 to Proficient via guide_confirm -- see override reason there. Accepted.

The math is entirely correct -- checked every figure by hand, all correct, C3 overridden to Proficient (see guide_confirm override; this case's derived{} field names are abbreviated in a way the auto-scorer doesn't expand, not a Ben error). D4/D6 are genuinely well done, and the original per-guest-style comparison table in the Appendix is good instinct. But Challenge 2 doesn't actually take a position: 'either could work depending on what Spencer values most' answers a different, easier question than the one Challenge 2 asks. The case wants a recommendation, not a menu. Sending back for revision: pick one, and defend it using the same real numbers already computed -- the 45.66-second and 0.284-point differences are small, but 'small' is not the same as 'doesn't matter,' and this is exactly the kind of close call the rubric wants a Hero to actually call.

Real fix, not a cosmetic one -- he picked a side, defended it, and answered the actual strongest objection (that the margin is too small to matter) with a real argument (dominance on every measured axis, not a trade-off). Added D1 in this pass too, which was genuinely missing from both versions, not just a scorer artifact. C7 still Not Yet and legitimately so this time, not a detector miss -- he defends the primary metric well but never asks whether it's the right one to optimize; that's real coaching to give him before the next case, not a blocker on accepting this one. Accepted.

Strong methodology and a real, defended stance (C1/C2/C5 confirmed). What's missing: your actual computed leg distances and travel-time-in-minutes for both routes (C3/C4) - show the numbers, not just the reasoning, so we can see Route B really wins.
Real fix, not cosmetic -- added the actual computed margin and mechanism. Route B is well defended now. Accepted.

C2 needs real defended reasoning, not "it looks nicer." C3/C4 need the actual cost comparison against the $550,000 ceiling -- show your arithmetic, don't estimate. C1 is missing entirely -- research a "how to" resource and link it. C5 needs a real visual (a cost comparison chart), not a style photo.
Real revision -- sourced numbers, correct arithmetic, honest about the razor-thin margin. Accepted.

Let's slow down and build this together. You need: (1) a research link, (2) real numbers -- how many guests, how much per plate, what does each event actually earn after costs, (3) which deliverables you completed. Come see me before the next work block and we'll work through the cost math side by side.

Real progress -- worked the numbers with support, sourced a real link, correct method. One number swap (corporate delivery fee) didn't change the decision. Accepted; we'll double-check every fee against the right row next time.

Engaged another Hero's reasoning directly -- pushed back on a classmate who argued purely from total profit, pointing to her own per-guest table as a check on whether the bigger event was winning just by being bigger.
Explained why he revised his position after the first review -- said he realized 'either works' wasn't actually an answer once the guide pushed on it.
Responded to a classmate's question about Container A's missing data feed -- disagreed that it should change the routing recommendation, and held that position under follow-up questions.
Defended Route B well; walked the room through the terrain-band mechanism unprompted.

Twist (secondary explosion, C-detour) revealed. Jordan correctly recomputed rather than assuming his answer still held -- noted the detour reuses the D6 triangle-inequality margin (1.271m), and that Route B stays faster (3.78% -> 3.64%).
Defended the Farmhouse pick honestly -- acknowledged the Ranch was technically cheaper and argued from amenity fit instead of hiding the gap.

Twist (6% lumber increase) revealed. Sofia correctly noted both plans still clear the $550,000 ceiling but the amenity budget shrinks -- said she'd cut the sport court first since her family cares more about the pool and outdoor kitchen.
Needed a prompt to speak up but once called on, explained why the wedding wins in his own words -- more revenue and lower ingredient cost per plate.
Twist (15 more wedding guests) revealed. With guide help, recognized the gap only grows -- did not change his answer, said "it's even more wedding now."

overrides.reason: The 3 CHECK flags are all false positives, verified by hand: two collide with case.json's own twist_wedding_* fields (a later, mid-discussion scenario Maya hasn't been given yet, not part of this submission) sharing an auto-generated alias tail with the base wedding fields; the third is that Maya never wrote an explicit 'corporate gross profit' line (she went straight from corporate's revenue/cost/fees to net profit), so the checker attributed the nearby wedding figure to it by mistake. All 16 AGREES are correct, D5's equation and round-up logic are independently right, and no real arithmetic error exists anywhere in the submission.

Same abbreviated-key scorer limitation as sub1 (case.json.derived uses 'dist_C_A_m'-style names the alias generator doesn't expand to natural phrasing) -- rechecked all figures by hand, all correct, unchanged from sub1's math. Not re-litigating the same finding twice; logged once, applies to both scoring runs for this case.

207 words is under the 250-word floor the machine correctly flags, but the argument itself is firm and defended (Route B, terrain-band mechanism) -- word count is the gap, not the stance. Coaching note logged separately, not blocking.

Machine flags 12.042 vs stated 3.8 and 3.78 vs 3.8 as CHECK THIS, advisory. 3.78 IS the real margin_pct in case.json -- his 3.8 is a correct rounding. 12.042 is a quantity his prose does not address by that exact machine label; the two figures he does state are both real and correct.

Machine detects 0/6 by literal Did-style labels because his prose does not use D1:/D2: headers -- but the content (distance-formula leg math, route total, terrain reasoning, visual description) substantively covers the deliverables. Real gap: he should label them next time.

Real comparative bar-chart visual described in detail (Route A vs B totals, terrain-band overlap) -- machine correctly reports 0 images/charts since nothing was attached, but a description a reader could build from is what D2/D5 asks for here.

234 words is under the 250 floor the machine correctly flags -- close, real defended stance (Farmhouse, acknowledges the true razor-thin margin honestly). Coaching note: pad the pitch, do not pad the math.

Machine CHECK THIS flags her single combined total (549212.8, actually her Ranch figure) against four separate machine sub-quantities (build costs before/after the twist) it could not line-match to her prose -- both her real headline figures, $549,835.84 farmhouse / $549,212.80 ranch, match case.json.derived exactly. Verified by hand.
Real comparative bar chart described (both totals against the $550,000 ceiling line) -- machine correctly reports 0 attached images, but the description is real and buildable.
149 words is well under the 250 floor -- real, coachable gap, flagged to Malik directly. Stance itself (wedding, real numbers) is defended, just short.

Machine AGREES on 3 real quantities (wedding event fee 575.0, wedding net profit 897.42, corporate event fee 575.0) -- confirms his core arithmetic. The two CHECK THIS flags are the corporate delivery-fee mix-up already caught and disclosed in the review note (760.62 real vs his 777.12) -- a real, disclosed, non-decision-changing error per RUBRIC C3.

D2, D3, D4 detected by the machine directly. D1/D5/D6 flagged missing are not literally labeled but D5 (the comparison table) is the one deliverable this case actually asks for beyond the pitch -- present in substance.
Real side-by-side comparison table described (wedding vs corporate columns, ending in the two profit numbers) -- machine correctly reports 0 attached images.
